_readme: Operator-gathered evidence for one frozen release SHA, in the shape
scripts/release_gate.py consumes: one key per gate, each carrying the
release_sha it is bound to. Keys are ABSENT for gates nobody has proven —
check_external reports a missing key as UNVERIFIED, which blocks, and that
is the honest answer. Never add a key to make a gate go green.
8ebc2e4 is the first SHA carrying migration 032 as an APPLIED migration
rather than a committed file, so it is the first one the dead_man gate can
be bound to at all. The previous evidence file (ccbdfe0) omitted that key
on purpose and said why.
OMITTED ON PURPOSE, and why:
restore  - Supabase's only restore path provisions a NEW billed project.
That is the account owner's call, not something to spend for
a drill without asking. Unchanged since ccbdfe0.
rollback - the documented one-command rollback needs a Render deploy hook
stored as RENDER_DEPLOY_HOOK_URL. That secret does not exist,
so the procedure in docs/DISASTER_RECOVERY.md has never been
executed end to end and must not be claimed.
backup   - PASSED at ccbdfe0 on a reading taken 2026-08-14T12:54Z. It is
NOT re-verified here: this session has no tool that lists
Supabase backups, and a property that was true six hours ago
is not evidence about this SHA. Re-verifying means the
project's Database > Backups page, which is Eric's console.
The last confirmed reading stays in the ccbdfe0 file.

dead_man.detail: Drilled, not asserted — docs/RELEASE.md section 3. Migration 032 applied to production 2026-08-14T14:26Z; pg_cron is installed and job 'ops-dead-man-sweep' is scheduled '*/10 * * * *'. (1) Registered a heartbeat with a 1s interval and no grace. (2) The sweep filed it: dedup_key dead_man:release_drill, status open, failure_state 'blocked' (never once seen, not merely late), detail.overdue_seconds 37, detected_by ops_dead_man_sweep. (3) Checked in and swept again: the same incident went status resolved, failure_state 'recovered', 3 rows on ops_incident_events — the outage stayed on the record. (4) Dropped the drill row. Separately, record_ops_heartbeat('no_such_heartbeat') returned false and created nothing, so a typo'd workflow surfaces as a missing heartbeat rather than a new row that satisfies nothing. Both halves of the mutual watch are live: pg_cron has run the sweep 15 times with 0 failures (last 2026-08-14T16:50:00Z), and the daily ops-scan reads the sweep's own heartbeat — it reported {"installed":true,"overdue":false,"judged_by_clock":"database"} at 15:13:29Z, having reported installed:false and filed an urgent incident that same morning. That incident was auto-resolved by the first real sweep, which is the design working end to end rather than a claim about it.

open_incidents.detail: Counted directly against the production table at 2026-08-14T16:50Z: select count(*) from ops_incidents where status not in ('resolved','suppressed'). Eleven of the twelve share ONE root cause, established by probe rather than inferred: the failing seeds for jhu, princeton, stanford and uva all return Cloudflare 403, three of them with cf-mitigated: challenge. Both a Shanghai residential egress and a GitHub-hosted runner are blocked on the same URLs, so this is UA/TLS fingerprinting rather than IP reputation, and campus_graph has no headless crawl strategy (static/recursive/rss/sitemap only) to answer it with. Nothing here was resolved or suppressed to shorten the list.
